title: Testing Library
description: Test utilities for DOM and component testing.

data.text: Testing Library provides utilities to test components from the user's perspective. It encourages accessible and maintainable tests.

data.title: Testing Library example

data.text: Query by Role, Not by Test Id

React Testing Library renders a component into the DOM and gives you queries that match how a user finds things: `getByRole`, `getByLabelText`, `getByText`. That pushes tests toward accessible markup, because a button that has no accessible name is hard to query — and hard for a screen reader.

data.title: Render and interact like a user

data.text: Async Utilities and the Screen Object

`findBy*` queries return a promise and wait for the element to appear, which is the right tool after an async update. `waitFor` retries an assertion until it passes or times out. `screen` queries the whole document, so you rarely need the destructured result of `render`.

data.title: Waiting for async content
Interview angle: test what the user sees
data.text: The library deliberately removed `shallow` rendering and deep component-instance access. The philosophy is that tests should survive a refactor: if you only change how a component is implemented, a test querying by visible text and role should still pass. Interviewers look for that reasoning, plus the rule of preferring `getByRole` and falling back to `getByTestId` only when nothing else is queryable.
